front.title: Agent Passports and Delegation Receipts for Autonomous Software Agents

abstract.t:
Autonomous software agents call APIs, tools and other agents on behalf of people and organisations. A party receiving such a call today can usually learn only that some bearer credential was presented. It cannot learn which organisation is accountable for the agent, which model, configuration and tools the agent is running, on whose behalf it is acting, or whether any of that has changed since it was approved.
This document defines two signed objects and how they travel on HTTP requests. An Agent Passport binds an agent's public key to its accountable controller and to a digest of its build. A Delegation Receipt records one step of authority passing from a principal, through a delegator, to an agent; a chain of receipts can only narrow that authority. Requests carry both, and are signed with the agent's key using HTTP Message Signatures, so a relying party can check, without contacting the issuer per request, who the agent is, what it is running, on whose behalf it acts and what it may do.
